predecessors.name: Mitanni
predecessors.text: Carchemish, which 'remained firmly under Mittanian control' (Suppiluliuma I page) until its siege and conquest c.

successors.name: Neo-Assyrian Empire
successors.text: 'Carchemish was conquered by Sargon II in 717 BC in the reign of King Pisiri'; the city and its lands 'turned into an Assyrian province'

ledger.x: c. 1345 BC: Suppiluliuma I takes Carchemish and makes it a kingdom. 'Carchemish was captured by king Suppiluliuma I of the Hittites' (c. 14th century BC; 'siege and conquest by Suppiluliuma I (c. 1345 BC)') and 'made it into a kingdom ruled by his son Piyassili' (table: c. 1315). The infobox says 'Established: c. 1321…

c. 1345 BC: Carchemish becomes a Hittite vassal kingdom. The Suppiluliuma I page: he 'besieged of Carchemish and finally captured it', 'installing his son Piyassili, also known as Sharri-Kushuh as its vassal king'; 'Carchemish, however, remained firmly under Mittanian control' before. The page gives no year.

c. 1175 BC: Kuzi-Teshub makes Carchemish independent. The table dates him 'c. 1170' and says he 'claimed the title of Great King after the fall of Hatti'; 'This powerful polity lasted from c. 1175 to 975 BC' and 'survived the Sea Peoples' attacks'.

c. 1175 BC (bridged): the Great Kingdom of Carchemish extends. The page says the post-1175 polity 'extended from Southeast Asia Minor to Northern Syria and the West bend of the Euphrates' without naming lands, dates or the ceded states; the Hittite lands left stateless are the bridge.

c. 975 BC (bridged): the Great Kingdom ends. 'This powerful polity lasted from c. 1175 to 975 BC.' The page names no cause and no lands lost; the area returns to the district round Carchemish (Houses of Suhi, early 10th century, and of Astiruwa).

c. 975 BC: the Great Kingdom becomes the ordinary Neo-Hittite kingdom of the House of Suhi. 'Suhi I ruled in early 10th century BC', Katuwa 'reigned around 880 BC', 'King Sangara (870-848 BC)', 'king Astiruwa (ca 848-790 BC) was the founder of this dynasty'. Same state, same colour (rule 2).

c. 870 BC (bridged): Sangara pays tribute to Assyria. 'Sangara paid tribute to Kings Ashurnasirpal II and Shalmaneser III' - 'at some time before 868 BC' per the Balawat Bands; Sangara's reign begins 870. The page gives no year for either tribute.
717 BC: Sargon II ends the tributary state.
717 BC: Carchemish becomes an Assyrian province.
717 BC: the kingdom of Carchemish ends under Pisiri, its last king.

wars.name: Suppiluliuma I's siege of Carchemish
wars.outcome: Carchemish captured after a siege and given to Piyassili as vassal king.

wars.name: Sargon II's conquest of Carchemish
wars.outcome: Pisiri's uprising defeated; Carchemish an Assyrian province.

certainty.note: No Carchemish boundary is given on any page; the Euphrates west bank and the Turkey-Syria frontier are only the site's setting.
